description: WO-E4. THE ADDON IS THE ADAPTER. Blender 4.2.23 is launched headless with the shipped zip installed; enabling it runs adapter/host_hook.py::declare(), which validates the addon's own static HostRegistration through the SDK's register_host() and writes scruple-host.json; then bpy.ops.scruple.host_announce writes one document per generation from bpy datablocks. Nothing in this repository writes either file. The gate is unchanged from WO-D6 — it still observes a wire, and a wire still cannot carry 'this was scene X at frame Y through camera Z, EEVEE at 1920x1080'. The driver chose the scene name, the frame and the camera; it did NOT choose the engine, the resolution, the sample count or the file format, and those are on the leaf too.

THE GATE OF THIS WORK ORDER. Three-valued and inside the MAC: blind (nobody to ask), declined (asked, nothing to say), supplied.
so a batch of leaves from a known-bad addon build can be found. The adapter id is separate from the host because one Blender has several: this is the ComfyUI bridge, not the render queue.

⚑ THE WHOLE OF LEVEL 2. This string was given to Blender, set on a bpy scene datablock, read back out of it by the addon, written to a file before the app was launched — and the gate could not have known it: a wire carries bytes and a graph, not a scene name.

auditNote:
The five mutations are the five ways a Blender deployment can end up with nothing, or the wrong thing, on a leaf — and the point of the design is that NO TWO OF THEM READ THE SAME.

`no-host-adapter` is the work order's first control: the addon absent. The gate never sees a host directory, the leaf reads `blind`, and every Level-2 assertion goes red while the artifact, its leaf and the model fingerprints do not move. Level 1 loses meaning, never coverage.

`no-announcement` is the second, and it is the one the work order calls the one that matters: the addon IS there and said nothing about THIS generation. `declined`, not `blind`. It reddens the document assertions and leaves `leaf-names-the-host` GREEN — naming the host is a fact about the deployment that stays true when an announcement is missing. An operator reading `declined` goes and looks at the add-on; an operator reading `blind` goes and installs one.

`partial-announcement` drops `camera` from a document the addon wrote, which is the third control: a document that fails the host's OWN declared schema. It is DECLINED and the decline is RECORDED with its reason, and the run continues with full Level-1 coverage. ⚑ The addon itself will not produce this document — `host_hook.announce()` checks presence AND type against the same schema and writes nothing when it fails, which is why the mutation has to make one.

`announce-under-a-different-id` is the correlation control. The host chooses the prompt id, so it can get it wrong: here it announces a real, complete, schema-valid document about a real scene under one id and submits the generation under another. The leaf must say LESS — `declined`, no document, no hash — and must not say something FALSE. Nothing matches loosely, so choosing the id grants nothing.

`forge-the-declaration` is the registration control. A host declares what it is, never how good it is: an `attestation` key is refused by registerHost(), the run continues at Level 1, and the refusal is recorded rather than swallowed.

`model-swap` is WO-D4's, unchanged, and reddens exactly one assertion — the second adapter in the sink chain did not disturb the first.

AND NOTE WHAT SEPARATES THEM. `no-declaration-was-refused` is GREEN under `no-host-adapter` and RED under `forge-the-declaration`. `leaf-names-the-host` is GREEN under `no-announcement`, `partial-announcement` and `announce-under-a-different-id`, and RED under the two that leave nobody registered.
